source.title: Domain-specific impairment in metacognitive accuracy following anterior prefrontal lesions

confidence_rationale: The second causal dissociation this directory now holds, and the one that generalises Lak et al. 2014 from rat to human and from pharmacological inactivation to structural lesion: anterior prefrontal lesion patients (n=7) showed selectively impaired perceptual metacognitive accuracy (meta-d'/d' 95% CI 0.28-0.64) while performing the first-order task equivalently to a temporal-lobe lesion comparison group (n=11) and healthy controls (n=19). It carries a second and more distinctive challenge the directory did not previously have: the deficit was domain-specific, sparing metacognition on an equivalent memory task (meta-d'/d' 95% CI 0.78-1.29), which is awkward for a single architecture-wide V(t) available on a shared bus. Confidence 0.64 rather than higher because first-order performance equivalence is partly a design requirement (difficulty was matched) rather than a discovered sparing, because n=7 with heterogeneous non-experimental lesions is weak causal evidence, and because the task is again a 2AFC perceptual discrimination whose trajectory space is degenerate -- the same scope limit that keeps Lak et al. from being a refutation.
failure_signatures: ARC-055 asserts V(t) must be available to and influence E3 selection. Here the explicit metacognitive signal was measurably degraded by anterior prefrontal lesion while first-order task performance was statistically indistinguishable from two control groups. This is the Lak et al. 2014 dissociation reproduced in humans with a different lesion method and a different metacognitive measure, which materially raises the cost of dismissing the pattern as preparation-specific.

The domain-specificity is a distinct and arguably sharper problem for the claim. ARC-055 posits V(t) and D_V as architecture-level signals available to E3 selection AND to E1 state representation AND to the E2 transition model AND to learning-update prioritisation -- a single quantity on a shared bus with several consumers. Metacognitive accuracy fractionating by domain (perception impaired, memory spared, same patients) instead suggests confidence-like signals are computed and consumed locally per-domain. If REE implements one global V(t) where biology implements several local ones, the architectural commitment is mis-specified independently of whether the E3 leg holds.

Taken with Lak et al. 2014 and read against Masset et al. 2020 -- which reported an abstract, modality-general confidence signal in OFC -- the directory now contains an internal tension about whether the confidence-like signal is global or fractionated. That tension is unresolved and governance should see it as such rather than as a net-of-signs aggregate.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Patients with lesions to anterior prefrontal cortex (n=7) showed a selective deficit in perceptual metacognitive accuracy (meta-d'/d', 95% CI 0.28-0.64) despite performing the first-order perceptual task equivalently to a temporal-lobe lesion comparison group (n=11) and healthy controls (n=19), while their metacognitive accuracy on an equivalent memory task remained unimpaired (meta-d'/d', 95% CI 0.78-1.29). The temporal-lobe group was intact in both domains. The authors conclude that anterior prefrontal cortex plays a causal role in perceptual metacognition and that the neural architecture of metacognition, though often considered global and domain-general, comprises domain-specific components.
mapping.ree_translation: This entry does two things to ARC-055, and the second is the more interesting. The first is that it reproduces the Lak et al. 2014 dissociation in a different species, with a different causal method, and with a better metacognitive measure: degrade the explicit confidence signal and first-order choice carries on unaffected. One such dissociation could be dismissed as a quirk of rat temporal wagering; two, converging across rodent pharmacological inactivation and human structural lesion, make the pattern harder to write off, and they raise the evidential burden on ARC-055's assertion that V(t) must be available to E3. The second and more distinctive problem is domain-specificity. ARC-055 does not merely claim that a confidence-like signal exists; it claims that V(t) and D_V are explicit signals available to E3 trajectory selection AND influencing E1 state representation AND predicted by the E2 transition model AND prioritising learning updates. That is one quantity on a shared bus with four consumers. What these patients show is metacognitive accuracy fractionating by domain within the same individuals -- perception impaired, memory spared. If confidence-like signals are computed and read locally per-domain rather than published globally, then REE's single architecture-wide V(t) is the wrong shape, and that objection bites regardless of whether the E3 leg survives. It also sits in unresolved tension with Masset et al. 2020 already in this directory, which reported an abstract and modality-general confidence signal in OFC feeding multiple consumers.
mapping.mapping_caveat: This entry bears on the SELECTION leg -- specifically against it -- and on the shared-bus architecture; it does not re-evidence the learning leg. The defence available to ARC-055 is the same one recorded in the Lak et al. entry and it applies with equal force here: a two-alternative perceptual discrimination has essentially no trajectory structure, so preserved first-order performance under a degraded confidence signal does not show that selection over EXTENDED trajectories would be preserved. This remains a weak test bed rather than a refutation, and the directory now contains two instances of the same weak test rather than one strong one. Three further limits pull the same way. First-order performance equivalence is partly a design requirement, since difficulty was titrated to match performance across groups, so the sparing is less of a discovered dissociation than it first reads. n=7 with naturally-occurring, heterogeneous, non-experimentally-placed lesions is weak causal evidence by the standards of the other entries here. And metacognitive accuracy as measured by meta-d'/d' is a property of the correspondence between confidence REPORTS and performance -- it is a report measure, so strictly this shows the reporting pathway degraded, not that a selection-available signal was removed.
mapping.source_context: Human patients with anterior prefrontal cortex lesions (n=7) versus temporal lobe lesion comparison group (n=11) and healthy controls (n=19), performing matched perceptual and memory tasks with trial-by-trial confidence ratings; metacognitive accuracy quantified as meta-d'/d'.

confidence_components.notes: Source quality 0.76: Brain, with a genuinely strong design for a lesion study -- a lesion comparison group as well as healthy controls, two matched domains within the same patients, and meta-d'/d' rather than raw confidence as the dependent measure. Held down by n=7 and by the non-experimental, heterogeneous nature of human lesions. Mapping fidelity 0.62, weighted heavily per the arch_commitment convention and the lowest of the four entries added in this pull: meta-d'/d' is a report-accuracy measure and the first-order sparing is partly built into the difficulty matching, so the entry speaks to ARC-055's E3 leg only through the same indirect route as Lak et al. Its domain-specificity finding maps onto the shared-bus commitment more directly and cleanly than its dissociation maps onto the selection leg. Transfer risk 0.40. Aggregate 0.64: filed 'weakens' because both of its findings run against the claim as written, but deliberately not higher, because a 2AFC preparation is the wrong instrument for testing a claim about selection among extended trajectories and the directory should not accumulate confidence from repeating a weak test.
